Nadir is an innovative SME founded in 2008 by a group of researchers with over 10 years of experience in the nanotechnology sector who have worked as scientific consultants in the field of technology transfer between academia and industry. Since 2016 Nadir has focused its activity on the application of an innovative and proprietary atmospheric plasma technology and in the development of advanced polymer composites. Since 2020 Nadir has been recognized as a "key innovator" by the EC Innovation radar initiative (https://www.innoradar.eu/innovator/972500079 ). 
The company, after applying for an international patent on the new atmospheric plasma device, has obtained the related grants in countries such as the United States, China, Japan, Australia, Europe and Canada. 
The Nadir Plasma device is now entering in various application sectors ranging from advance manufacturing, biomedical, aerospace, electronics and 3D printing, for cleaning treatments, surface activation, deposition of functional coatings and metallic layers and improvement of adhesion between dissimilar materials. 
Similarly, the advanced polymeric materials proposed by Nadir, such as electro-conductive, responsive, antimicrobial and improved performance polymers, as well as being studied in various European projects, are now applied in the sectors indicated above. Currently the company has its operational headquarters in Venezia-Mestre (Italy), with a Plasma laboratory equipped for the design and development of new devices and the study of innovative surface treatment processes, and with a Polymers laboratory equipped with different melt compounding technologies for the study of new generations of active and bioactive fillers for the production of advanced polymer composites.

Pulsar Space Intelligence is a French deep-tech startup specializing in space environment risk mitigation for satellite operators. 
Our mission is to make satellite operations more resilient and cost-effective in the increasingly congested and disturbed low Earth orbit (LEO) environment.
We develop and operate a global network of passive ground sensors combined with a real-time digital twin of the near-Earth space environment. 
Our proprietary system fuses space weather forecasting, orbital traffic monitoring, and RF beacon tracking to deliver predictive alerts, maneuver recommendations, and environmental analytics.

Pulsar’s services enable satellite operators to:
- Reduce downtime caused by space weather and collision risks,
- Optimize fuel consumption for orbital maneuvers,
- Lower insurance premiums through better risk management,
- Extend mission lifetimes and delay costly satellite replacements.

Our core technological expertise spans:
- Radio frequency (RF) signal processing,
- Space weather modeling and prediction,
- Orbital mechanics and conjunction analysis,
- Machine learning for anomaly detection and forecasting.

Founded by engineers (Valentin STEE) and scientists (Anthony SALSI) with backgrounds in aerospace, space physics, and signal intelligence, Pulsar collaborates with leading academic institutions such as "Observatoire de la Cote d'Azur" and targets customers in the NewSpace industry, defense, public agencies, and satellite insurance sectors.

LA composite, s.r.o. (company limited) was founded in 1995 as joint venture of companies Letov, a.s. and ATG, s.r.o.. Later on, ATG, s.r.o. acquired the Letov's share and became an exclusive owner of LA composite.Since then, we have been continuing in the long-standing tradition of manufacturing of composite, sandwich and bonded structures for aerospace industry. Meanwhile, our range of product expanded into the terrestrial transport industry (railway vehicles, automotive) and into other applications (yachts, textile industry etc).We offer our customers wide range of complex services from design up to serial production of parts. 

LAC specializes in the production of composite parts using state-of-the-art technologies. A key part of our manufacturing process is autoclave curing, ensuring maximum strength and quality of the final products. We work with advanced resin systems, including epoxy, phenolic, and BMI, and focus on precision in every detail. Production takes place in climate-controlled clean rooms with laser projection for perfect material layering. For final processing, we utilize high-precision 5-axis CNC machining, and to maintain optimal material properties, we have a large-capacity freezing storage. By combining cutting-edge technology with years of expertise, we deliver top-tier composite solutions for the most demanding applications.

LAC represents: 
• Czech private company 
• 100% owned by ATG (Advanced Technology Group) – Czech company with core business in Non-destructive testing (NDT) 
• Approved EASA Part 21G and Part 145 organizations
• Established in 1995 (almost 25 years of experience in composite business) 
• Expertise in small and medium serious production 
• Staff: 65 employees 
• Turnover: 4.2 mil. EUR 
LAC supplies composite parts to aircraft and helicopters manufacturers in France, Germany, Italy and South Korea.
We take every effort to ensure top quality workmanship and provide individual approach to each customer. 
Our key advantage is our engineering team and scope of activities ranging from prototyping, serial production, tooling, treatment, assembly, finishing and quality control. 

(2) Facilities
LAC is based in Prague (in the aerospace area neighboring ATG’s customers GE Aviation and Latecoere). 
Our facility is equipped with 2 autoclaves, 2 ovens, 5 axis CNC machine and prepreg cutting machines, clean room with control parameters, freezing storage rooms, assembly room and others. 

(3) Core Business and Field of Activities
LAC Core Business is in the aerospace industry. The main capabilities are in the production of structural and interior parts according to technical documentation (as a “Build-to-Print“ manufacturer).
Our key technology is based on prepreg technology with curing in autoclaves. LAC has expertise with various materials in composite production. 
LAC also supplies its customers with additional services such as engineering, production of molds and fixtures, cutting, drilling holes, milling, assembly with metallic parts, rivets, bolts, painting (together with approved supplier), marking, testing etc.
 
LAC Secondary Business is in Maintenance, Repairs and Overhaul (MRO). LAC participates on repairs and upgrades of aircraft composite components for various customers together with ATG (mother company) and its complete NDT service package. 
LAC also conducts several modification of interior parts and the Company introduced new product - so called C-Spacer (class divider) for Boeing 737 cabin with its DOA partner. 
 
Additionally, LAC engineering skills support completely new aircraft structure. 
Together with partners, LAC develops and manufactures prototypes of composite aircraft including composite wings. The Company contributes to making a prototype of advanced civil helicopters with development of composite engine mounts. 
There are more R&D projects (in space industry as well) with involvement of LAC such as state-of-the-art ballistic protection, space applications – shielding, panels, etc. 

(4) Main Customers and Certifications
LAC has more than 15 years of on-going cooperation with Airbus Helicopters. LAC produces fire protection lining across Airbus aircraft family (A320, A320neo, A330, A350, A380). 
These parts are delivered to both Germany and South Korea for final assembly with door structures. For helicopter manufacturers, LAC produces composite bays/covers for both life raft and floatation systems. 
Other customers include: Leonardo Helicopters, Daher, Diehl and Korean Air.
LAC approvals: ISO EN ISO 9001:2015, AS 9100, rev. D, EN 9100:2018, EASA Part 21-G and EASA Part 145
LAC customers approvals: Airbus, Airbus Helicopters, Korean Air, Agusta Westland QRS01, Daher Socata IS18S13, Diehl Aviation

Get2C was founded in 2011, leveraging more than 20 years of experience of its founders and team.
We work in the areas of climate change, energy, carbon markets, climate finance and sustainable development.
We have a global culture and are present in various countries in Europe, Africa and Latin America through our network of partners.

“Develop Smart Projects into a Cooler World” – materializes in the implementation of environmentally, socially and economically sustainable projects that lead us towards a cooler world.

We know it’s a long road and we’ll have to rethink the concept of efficiency in the use of natural resources. We believe that we have to define new patterns of services, consumption, production and behavior so that the concept of “less carbon” is not just a combination of two words. We know that we have to look at problems in an innovative and integrated way in collaboration, cooperation and partnership. Only in this way will we create future value in order to achieve a low-carbon economy.

We know it’s a path we want to take! A path that will lead us to a “Cooler World” with zero emissions by the second half of the century.

According to NASA’s Earth Observatory, the average global temperature on Earth has risen by around 1.04° Celsius since 1880. Two-thirds of the warming has occurred since 1975, at a rate of around 0.15-0.20°C per decade.

Although the results of the Copenhagen conference in 2009 fell short of expectations, it was the first time that the final text recorded the international commitment to a maximum limit of 2 degrees Celsius for the increase in the Earth’s average temperature in the future.

It is in this scenario, in which the average global temperature would rise by a maximum of 2 degrees Celsius, that Get2C drew inspiration. Although the impacts are already negative with this rise, the aim is to minimize them and create opportunities to seriously limit a global temperature increase of more than 2 degrees Celsius.

Get2C is committed to having a culture that involves the best of its employees and helps mobilize external partners. This commitment gives them the opportunity to use their skills, resources and management capacity to drive social progress, engaging with the community and new partners.
We are committed to being a Cool company by fostering an inspiring culture that encourages creativity, keeps employees happy and motivated, and promotes the development of qualities and professional fulfillment balanced with personal life.

description:
FWR is developing a new generation of electric robotic arms for advanced manipulation and simple deployment in ANY existing environment. Although our robots are supposed to do what electric robots do, and certainly with some enhanced qualities, their distinguishing feature lies in their remote Actuation Box. This box houses all the critical components of the system – electronics, sensors and even electric motors – protecting them from any environmental factors, such as radiations, water, extreme temperatures, flammable gasses and dust (including regolith, why not). Therefore, reliability in challenging environments is unconditionally achieved as:
- the robotic arm is basically a simple, passive, and lightweight structure, free of any delicate/fragile components, and
- the Actuation Box offers effective cooling, shielding and sealing of critical components without affecting the properties of the arm structure (such as weight/inertia, shape/size, design complexity), which would not be possible relying on traditional design approaches.
Although remote actuation architecture can easily be considered as the ideal candidate for achieving reliability in harsh environments, its implementation is not straightforward due to the intrinsic challenges of developing transparent transmission systems capable of transferring the motion of the remote electric motors to the corresponding arm joints. Indeed, no state-of-the-art robot with remote actuation has yet demonstrated a suitable balance of performance, reliability, and low complexity. As a result, scalability, versatile deployment, and mass distribution of this kind of system remain unfeasible, ultimately making the benefits of remote actuation vanish.
With this exact problem in mind, we are developing Fluid Wires – flexible, fluidic transmission systems – presumably the most advanced transmission system for robotics, capable of making robots with remote actuation ready for real-world deployment and industrialization for the first time. Unlike existing transmission systems, Fluid Wires offer near-zero friction, large force-control bandwidth, and high load capacity, combining the efficiency of electric actuation (powering our system from within the box) with the high specific power of hydraulic systems. As a reminder, note that the proposed technology should not be mistaken for traditional hydraulic robots (with pumps, valves, etc.); our robots are fully electric in all aspects, with motors placed remotely and connected via fluidic transmissions. Additionally, considering the low inertia of our robotic arm – an almost empty structure – the proposed architecture enables high dynamic performance, allowing for fast movements with efficiency and good controllability. Moreover, the extreme transparency of Fluid Wires (low friction, high bandwidth) enables the electric motors to also function as torque sensors, eliminating the need for force/torque sensors, which are typically costly and prone to failure. Unlike traditional, highly geared robotic arms, which necessarily require torque or force sensors to implement impedance-control strategies, FWR robots enable sensorless force/impedance control in an accurate, robust, and impact-tolerant manner. This makes them particularly suitable for safe navigation (e.g., inspection, maintenance, assembling, and teleoperation) in unstructured environments. As a final remark, all the favorable characteristics analyzed above are implemented with simplified hardware. Fluid Wires are flexible and can be seamlessly integrated into the robotic structure. The design of the arm and the one of the Actuation Box are decoupled, offering significant design freedom to meet the project requirements, and our architecture is fully modular (with the same design and components applied to every joint), resulting in lower design and manufacturing costs, as well as easy customization.
Performance, safety and reliability, which traditionally belong to different families of robots, are merged here into a unified advanced design paradigm and embedded in smart mechanical structures, without trade-offs.
